'''Mato Grosso Arára''' (also disambiguated as ''Arara do Beiradão'' or ''Arara do Rio Branco'', and also known as ''Koaiá ~ Koayá'' or ''Yugapkatã''<ref name="Ramirez-2010">Ramirez, Henri. 2010. [http://www.etnolinguistica.org/biblio:ramirez-2010-etnonimos Etnônimos e topônimos no Madeira (séculos XVI-XX): um sem-número de equívocos]. ''Revista Brasileira de Linguística Antropológica'' v. 2 n. 2, p. 179-224. ([http://www.etnolinguistica.org/local--files/biblio:ramirez-2010-etnonimos/Ramirez_2010_Etnonimos_e_toponimos_no_Madeira.pdf PDF])</ref>) is an [[extinct language|extinct]] [[unclassified language]] of [[Brazil]]. The ethnic population that spoke the language numbers 249 as of 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arara do Rio Branco - Povos Indígenas no Brasil |url=https://pib.socioambiental.org/pt/Povo:Arara_do_Rio_Branco |access-date=2025-06-21 |website=pib.socioambiental.org}}</ref>

==Classification==
The language is unclassified, with no known connections to established families. It is attested in a single word list, which shows it is neither [[Tupian]] nor [[Arawakan]]. Four people remembered the language in 2001, and two in 2008, but none were fluent speakers.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hammarström |first=Harald |date=September 2015 |title=Ethnologue 16/17/18th editions: A comprehensive review: Online appendices |url=https://muse.jhu.edu/article/593411 |journal=Language |language=en |volume=91 |issue=3 |pages=s1–s188 |doi=10.1353/lan.2015.0049 |issn=1535-0665|hdl=11858/00-001M-0000-0029-1D58-0 |hdl-access=free |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Jolkesky (2010) notes some lexical similarities with [[Tupian languages|Tupian]].<ref name=":0">Jolkesky, Marcelo. 2010. ''[https://www.academia.edu/5311702/Arara_do_Rio_Branco_e_o_tronco_Tup%C3%AD Arara do Rio Branco e o tronco Tupí]''.</ref>
